chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, all of them, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Sunnah has established that the Jizyah (poll tax) is not taken from the 'Ma'tuh (one who is insane/mentally deficient) nor from the one whose intellect is overpowered (by insanity).

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: The established practice or legal precedent
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةُ: The poll tax levied on non-Muslim subjects
key_terms.الْمَعْتُوهِ: The mentally deficient or insane person
key_terms.الْمَغْلُوبِ عَلَى عَقْلِهِ: One whose intellect is overpowered (by insanity)

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from paying Jizyah due to mental incapacity in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* codifies the exemption of the mentally incapacitated from Jizyah, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that fiscal obligations require full cognitive capacity (*'aql*). By distinguishing between the 'Ma'tuh and the 'Maghlub 'ala 'aqlihi, it ensures that those lacking the rational faculty to manage their affairs or understand the covenant are not burdened with this poll tax.
